answersReviewFindings.finding: 1. Expired copies used up the 20-copy drain budget, so fresh kept messages were not forwarded.
answersReviewFindings.fix: roleKeepDrainMax (20) now bounds forwards only; a second constant, roleKeepScanMax (200), bounds the walk, with its reason in a comment: a lane can hold nothing but copies past the window, since the stream keeps a copy 72 h against a one-hour keep window. An expired or undecodable copy costs a scan, not a forward.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestADrainSpendsItsBudgetOnForwardsRatherThanOnExpiredCopies; at the pre-change files it fails 'the drain forwarded [], want every copy still inside the keep window: [envoy.role.forward.kept-budget-22 … -28]'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 2. Two listeners draining one role both forwarded every copy, because the cursor was written once after the walk; the guard comment described a guard that did not exist. The same defect let envoy_role_kept_expired_total count one copy again on every re-walk.
answersReviewFindings.fix: claimKeptRoleCopy claims each copy before anything is done with it: it advances the cursor to that one copy's stored.Sequence under the compare-and-swap, carrying the returned sequence into the next iteration, and only the drain whose claim landed forwards, drops or passes over that copy. An error wrapping bus.ErrCursorMoved stops the drain at once, logged at debug, reporting nothing wrong. The doc states the cost: a process that dies between a claim and its forward loses that one copy rather than delivering it twice.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestTwoDrainsOfOneRoleHandEachKeptCopyToExactlyOneHolder; at the pre-change files all six copies fail with 'reached [ses_kept_drain_second ses_kept_drain_first]; a kept copy reaches exactly one holder'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 3. The drain skipped beforeForward (echo, repeat, delivery-mode capability) and a kept copy carried no sender stamp.
answersReviewFindings.fix: sendToRole stamps senderStamp onto the envelope before the first resolution, so the copy a keep stores carries the sender as a live delivery's forward does. keptRoleForwardAllowed runs beforeForward for each claimed copy with the role lane's own seen (dedupeCache.Seen || attemptCache.Seen): echo skipped, repeat dedupe, a delivery-mode refusal failed with the lane's delivery_failed exception, each under its own line; only forwardAllowed forwards. withPublishRoute in confirmed_test.go now wires the attemptCache that rig left nil.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAKeptRoleMessageCarriesTheSenderThePublishStamped (pre-change: 'the kept copy's sender is <nil>') and TestTheDrainJudgesAKeptCopyByTheRulesEveryForwardPathApplies, echo and unadvertised mode (pre-change: 'the drain forwarded the copy 1 times, want none' in both subtests).

answersReviewFindings.finding: 4. A role token rolePattern can never match was kept and answered 202, for a role no claim can take.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Keeping is (request.Keep == nil || *request.Keep) && isValidRole(role), with the reason at that line. Such a role gets exactly today's 404, byte for byte, with nothing stored; the 404 rather than a new 400, so no caller meets a status this route never gave it.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAPublishToARoleNoClaimCanNameIsRefusedAndKeepsNothing; at the pre-change files 'publish to a role no claim can name: status 202'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 5. A keep stored after a concurrent claim's drain had read the lane waited for a claim that seldom comes inside the hour.
answersReviewFindings.fix: drainAfterKeep: after a keep lands, on the publish route and on the role lane alike, the role's holder is resolved again by role delivery's rule (resolveRoleHolder with laneHolderFresh) under roleKeepHolderWindow (5 s), and a live holder is drained to. It runs off the request, so neither caller's answer waits; a resolution that failed logs at debug and changes nothing, since the copy is stored and the next claim still takes it.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAKeptCopyReachesTheHolderThatClaimedTheRoleUnderTheKeep; at the pre-change files 'the copy kept for ses_kept_under_claim, which held the role already, reached it in no 20 seconds'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 6. The role lane kept for a lapsed claim the restart grace retained, which no claim write ever drains.
answersReviewFindings.fix: One predicate, roleKeepable(roleHolderResult): keep for an unclaimed role, and for a lapsed claim unless store.ExpiredRoleClaimRetained. Both give-up paths call it, the publish route's first resolution included, so a retained claim keeps nothing and is answered exactly as before the kept lane: the lane's delivery_failed, the route's 404 holder_lapsed.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestTheRoleLaneKeepsNothingForAClaimTheRestartGraceRetained; at the pre-change files 'read delivery exception: nats: timeout', the lane having kept instead of excepting.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 7. The phase worker's stall notice to its architect lost its retry: a 202 marked it reported, so a notice nobody claimed the role for inside the hour was dropped.
answersReviewFindings.fix: tellArchitect sends keep: false and keeps its 404 retry, which is the case the design reserves the flag for: this sender's retry is the reminding itself, and reminders never stop while the phase is open. keptNothing is roleUnheld again with a true doc comment, and a 202 that reached it anyway is read as the 404 is, so the run's next reminder publishes again under the same key.
answersReviewFindings.test: 'a kept answer is not the architect being told, so the run's next reminder publishes again' (pre-change: expect(published[0]?.keep).toBe(false) receives undefined, and with the two keep assertions removed, reported: true where false is wanted), plus the 404 test, which now also pins keep: false on the wire.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 8. StreamSubjects() had become the stream's list, so every consumer filter had to remember DurableNotificationSubjects() and the tests no longer modelled the listener's filter.
answersReviewFindings.fix: streamSubjects and StreamSubjects() are the consumer list again, without the kept prefix, and durable.go calls it. streamCarriedSubjects (the consumer list plus KeptTopicPrefix + ">") is the stream's own, read by streamCfg.Subjects, StreamCaptures and the replay classification, exported as StreamCarriedSubjects() for a caller that builds or checks the stream, which is what bustest takes. DurableNotificationSubjects and its prefix filter are deleted. Every caller was re-read: the consumer filters needed no edit and now model the listener's filter correctly; the stream-modelling tests (internal/bus/keeper_test.go, adhoc_topic_test.go, bustest) moved to streamCarriedSubjects. TestStreamConfigExcludesRoleLanes and TestEveryStreamSubjectIsClassifiedForReplay read streamCfg.Subjects and are unchanged.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test: a refactor with no behaviour of its own, held by the suites above, which pass unchanged.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 9. Listener-only subjects lived in the shared contracts package with no TypeScript caller, hand-copied into the Go generator, so the string existed three times.
answersReviewFindings.fix: KeptTopicPrefix, KeptRoleSubject and KeptRoleCursorSubject are defined in internal/bus/stream.go beside ExceptionTopicPrefix and DeliverSubjectPrefix. The three TypeScript exports, their types, the gen-go.ts block and the generated Go are deleted, and pr2588-kept-subjects.yaml announces only the envelope's kept_at, which stays in contracts because both hosts read it.
answersReviewFindings.test: bun run check:go passes on the regenerated file, so the string exists once.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 10. A package-global guard map and a cfg == nil branch that existed only for tests.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The guard set is a roleKeepGuards field on listenerDeliveryHandlerConfig beside deferredUnplaceable, built once in main.go and in each harness, and listenerDeliveryHandler refuses a config without it as it refuses one without deferredUnplaceable. The global and both nil branches (startKeptRoleDrain's and drainAfterKeep's) are gone, and the rigs that claim a role through POST /v1/roles/set carry a delivery. The two-listener test gives the second drain a guard set of its own, which is what a second listener has.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test: held by the suites, and by the two-listener test, which no longer reaches into a global.

answersReviewFindings.finding: 11. The pull request body carried no contract change census for the publish route's 404 → 202 at a process boundary.
answersReviewFindings.fix: A '## Contract change census' section lists every caller of POST /v1/messages/publish for a role topic with its disposition: the five in this repository's production code (the client and the two envoy_publish tools adapted; the phase reminder and the daemon's notice publisher opted out with keep: false), the four scripts and live proofs (the rig adapted; three unaffected, each because it publishes to a role a live session holds), and the four hits outside it. theorem-labs/agent-infra holds no caller: two Pulumi.prod.yaml comments naming the route, one deployment-instructions page telling agents to reach roles with the envoy_publish tool (covered by the client), and one test that classifies a delivered frame. theorem-labs/nats-server has no hit for messages/publish, notifications.role or envoy_publish. The section ends with the rollout line.

trickyParts: Claiming each copy before forwarding it trades at-least-once for at-most-once: a drain that dies between its claim and its forward loses that one copy. That is the reviewer's and the architect's choice over two holders receiving one copy, and the drain's doc comment says so in those words.

drainAfterKeep resolves the holder again after a keep, which can release a lapsed claim as resolveRoleHolder always may. It runs off the request so neither caller's answer waits for it, and a resolution that failed changes nothing.

The two subject lists are a real distinction now and have to stay one: StreamSubjects() is what every consumer filter takes, StreamCarriedSubjects() is what builds or checks the stream. A test that models the listener's filter takes the first; one that models the stream takes the second.

dispatch://INFRA-392 (sjawhar/legion#2596) makes an unresponsive holder keep its claim and answer 404 holder_lapsed. Its architect and implementer have both confirmed that an unresponsive holder is always a RETAINED claim, so roleKeepable sends it down the unkept path and the two changes compose with neither undoing the other. Whichever merges second reconciles; I have told both.
deviations: Finding 4 is answered with today's 404 rather than the 400 the reviewer offered as an alternative, so no caller of this route meets a status it never gave.
